heuristics.rule: Apply for NSF GRFP in senior year of undergraduate study
heuristics.condition: When a US citizen, national, or permanent resident is in their final year of undergraduate study and intends to pursue a STEM PhD
heuristics.action: Submit NSF GRFP application before PhD enrollment to avoid the 12-month enrollment restriction
heuristics.because: NSF GRFP eligibility requires that the applicant has not been enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at time of application; applying as a senior undergrad avoids this restriction entirely
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP official documentation — eligibility criteria

heuristics.rule: Verify program CIP code with DSO before accepting admission offer
heuristics.condition: When an international student on F-1 is evaluating graduate programs and post-graduation work authorization
heuristics.action: Confirm the specific CIP code of the degree program with the Designated School Official (DSO) prior to accepting, not after
heuristics.because: STEM OPT extension (24 additional months) is available only for degrees on the STEM Designated Degree Program List as determined by CIP code, not program name; the difference is 12 months vs. 36 months of OPT
heuristics.regulatory_basis: ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List; standard OPT 12 months, STEM OPT extension 24 months

heuristics.rule: International PhD students must negotiate harder on institutional fellowship packages
heuristics.condition: When an international student is negotiating a PhD funding offer
heuristics.action: Explicitly ask each program what fellowship support is available to international students, and treat comparable domestic/international packages as effectively underfunding the international student
heuristics.because: International students cannot access the federal fellowship pool (NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART, Ford Foundation) that domestic students can, creating a structural funding asymmetry
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship — citizenship/residency eligibility requirements

heuristics.rule: Ask explicitly whether GRFP stipend is additive or substitutive before using fellowship as negotiating leverage
heuristics.condition: When a GRFP winner is negotiating with a PhD program
heuristics.action: Ask the department directly whether the GRFP $37,000 stipend and $16,000 cost-of-education allowance are additive to the standard package or substitute for department funding
heuristics.because: Not all departments count GRFP stipend toward their standard package; failure to ask may result in no net financial gain despite winning the fellowship
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP official documentation — strategic implications

heuristics.rule: Check for block grants and training grants at target programs
heuristics.condition: When a domestic STEM PhD applicant is evaluating funding at target programs
heuristics.action: Ask whether the program has NSF, NIH, or DoD training grants that provide guaranteed fellowship support to incoming students
heuristics.because: Block grants provide guaranteed institutional fellowship support independent of advisor grant availability, reducing funding risk
heuristics.regulatory_basis: NSF GRFP and federal fellowship program official documentation — fellowship strategy section

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines eligibility for all major US federal fellowship programs; international students on F-1/J-1 are excluded from NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Hertz Foundation, and Ford Foundation Predoctoral Fellowship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: US citizen, national, or permanent resident = eligible for federal fellowships; F-1/J-1 visa holders = excluded from all listed federal programs

decision_factors.factor: Enrollment duration at time of NSF GRFP application
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Applicants enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at time of application are ineligible for NSF GRFP
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Count months of PhD enrollment at time of application submission; must be 12 months or fewer, or not yet enrolled (final-year undergrad)

decision_factors.why_it_matters: Determines whether an international student qualifies for 24-month STEM OPT extension; program name is not determinative — only the CIP code matters
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Verify specific CIP code with DSO against the ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List; e.g., Computer Science CIP 11.07xx qualifies, Information Systems CIP 52.12xx does not

decision_factors.factor: Availability of institutional fellowships not tied to citizenship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: For international students who cannot access federal fellowships, institutional fellowships are the primary non-RA/TA funding source
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask each program explicitly what fellowship support is available to international students and whether any departmental fellowships are citizenship-neutral

decision_factors.factor: Whether GRFP stipend is additive or substitutive
decision_factors.why_it_matters: A GRFP award may not increase net funding if the department substitutes department funding with the fellowship amount
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly; there is no uniform policy — varies by department

decision_factors.factor: Field of study for NDSEG eligibility
decision_factors.why_it_matters: NDSEG is restricted to specific enumerated STEM fields; applicants in non-listed fields are ineligible regardless of citizenship
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Check whether the applicant's field is in the NDSEG list: aeronautical/astronautical engineering, biosciences, chemical engineering, chemistry, cognitive neuroscience, computer science, electrical engineering, geosciences, materials science, mathematics, mechanical engineering, naval architecture/ocean engineering, oceanography, physics

decision_factors.factor: Prior receipt of a federal graduate fellowship
decision_factors.why_it_matters: Prior receipt of a federal graduate fellowship disqualifies an applicant from NSF GRFP
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Has the applicant previously received any federal graduate fellowship? If yes, GRFP is not available

decision_factors.why_it_matters: RA funding is tied to advisor's grant availability (variable risk); TA funding is institutionally guaranteed; understanding the risk profile differs for planning and visa status stability
decision_factors.how_to_assess: Ask the program directly whether funding is through RA (grant-dependent) or TA (institutionally guaranteed); evaluate advisor's grant status

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Accepting a PhD offer with a package comparable to domestic students' offers
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: International students receiving packages equivalent to domestic students are structurally underfunded because domestic peers can supplement with NSF GRFP ($37,000/year), NIH NRSA, NDSEG, or other federal fellowships that international students cannot access
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International PhD students in STEM fields at programs that do not differentiate institutional offers by citizenship eligibility

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Winning NSF GRFP and enrolling in a PhD program
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: The financial benefit of GRFP may be zero if the department treats the fellowship as substitutive rather than additive to the standard package; the $37,000 GRFP stipend may simply replace department funding rather than supplement it
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: GRFP winners who do not explicitly ask about department policy before enrollment

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Selecting a graduate program based on program name or reputation without verifying CIP code
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: A degree program with a STEM-sounding name (e.g., Information Systems) may not qualify for STEM OPT extension if its CIP code falls outside the STEM Designated Degree Program List, limiting post-graduation work authorization to 12 months instead of 36 months
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: International students on F-1 visas in interdisciplinary or business-adjacent technology programs

hidden_tradeoffs.choice: Applying to NSF GRFP in first year of PhD rather than as a senior undergrad
hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: Using the first-year application as the first attempt consumes one of only two eligible application windows; a rejection in year one leaves only year two (second and final eligible window), with no recovery opportunity
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: US citizen/PR STEM students who delay their first GRFP application until after enrollment

hidden_tradeoffs.unstated_consequence: SMART Scholarship requires a post-graduation DoD employment commitment and summer internship obligations; recipients are not free to pursue academic or private-sector employment until the service commitment is fulfilled
hidden_tradeoffs.who_it_affects: STEM PhD students who accept SMART Scholarship without accounting for post-graduation career constraints

failure_patterns.pattern: International student applies for NSF GRFP
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: NSF GRFP explicitly requires US citizenship, national status, or permanent residency; F-1/J-1 visa holders do not meet the citizenship eligibility requirement
failure_patterns.consequence: Application ineligible; disqualification from NSF GRFP funding
warning_signs: Student is on F-1 or J-1 visa
Student assumes GRFP is open to all enrolled PhD students

failure_patterns.pattern: PhD applicant applies to NSF GRFP after being enrolled for more than 12 months
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: GRFP eligibility explicitly bars applicants who have been enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at time of application
failure_patterns.consequence: Application ineligible; permanent loss of GRFP eligibility if second-year window is also missed
warning_signs: Student has been in PhD program for over one year without applying
Student was unaware of the 12-month enrollment restriction

failure_patterns.pattern: International student discovers post-enrollment that their degree program CIP code does not qualify for STEM OPT extension
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: STEM OPT eligibility is determined by ICE/SEVP CIP code designation, not program name; students who do not verify CIP code with DSO before enrollment may be in non-qualifying programs
failure_patterns.consequence: Loss of 24-month STEM OPT extension; post-graduation work authorization limited to 12 months standard OPT
warning_signs: Student enrolled in an interdisciplinary or business-adjacent technology program
Student relied on program name rather than CIP code to assess STEM OPT eligibility
Student did not consult DSO before accepting offer

failure_patterns.pattern: Applicant who has previously received a federal graduate fellowship applies for NSF GRFP
failure_patterns.why_it_happens: GRFP eligibility explicitly bars applicants who have previously received a federal graduate fellowship
failure_patterns.consequence: Application ineligible; disqualification from NSF GRFP
warning_signs: Student previously held an NDSEG, SMART, or other federal graduate fellowship
Student did not check prior award history against GRFP exclusion criteria

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant a US citizen, national, or permanent resident?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Ford Foundation, and Hertz Foundation fellowships
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Proceed to evaluate enrollment duration and field eligibility for specific federal fellowship programs
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is excluded from all major US federal fellowship programs; focus on institutional fellowships, home country funding, and field-specific non-citizenship-restricted awards

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant been enrolled in a PhD program for more than 12 months at the time of NSF GRFP application?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for NSF GRFP; assess whether second-year window was already used
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant may be eligible; confirm no prior federal fellowship receipt

diagnostic_questions.question: Has the applicant previously received a federal graduate fellowship?
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant is ineligible for NSF GRFP
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Prior-award criterion does not bar application; proceed to other eligibility checks

diagnostic_questions.question: What is the CIP code of the degree program the international student is considering, and is it on the ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for 24-month STEM OPT extension, which determines total post-graduation work authorization (12 months vs. 36 months)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Student is eligible for STEM OPT extension; standard OPT 12 months + STEM OPT 24 months = 36 months total
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Student limited to 12 months standard OPT; immigration planning must account for shorter work authorization window

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the department treat GRFP stipend as additive or substitutive relative to the standard funding package?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Net financial benefit of GRFP to the student; determines whether GRFP award translates into higher actual compensation
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: GRFP is additive; student receives full GRFP stipend on top of standard package
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: GRFP is substitutive; student receives no net financial gain from GRFP award beyond potentially freeing up negotiating leverage on non-stipend dimensions

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant's field on the NDSEG eligible fields list?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: NDSEG fellowship eligibility; only specific enumerated STEM fields qualify
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may be eligible for NDSEG if also a US citizen or national (not permanent resident)
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Applicant is ineligible for NDSEG regardless of citizenship

diagnostic_questions.question: Does the target PhD program have institutional fellowships not tied to citizenship status?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Whether international students have access to non-RA/TA funding that domestic students access through federal fellowships
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: International student may be able to partially close the fellowship funding gap relative to domestic peers
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: International student is dependent entirely on RA/TA funding with no fellowship supplement; negotiate accordingly

diagnostic_questions.question: Is the applicant an immigrant or child of immigrants who is a permanent resident or US citizen?
diagnostic_questions.what_it_reveals: Eligibility for Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship for New Americans, which is one of the few prestigious fellowships accessible to eligible immigrants
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_yes: Applicant may qualify for Paul & Daisy Soros Fellowship; verify specific eligibility criteria
diagnostic_questions.follow_up_if_no: Soros Fellowship is not available; focus on other eligible fellowship categories

industry_realities.common_belief: A GRFP award automatically means more money in the PhD student's pocket
industry_realities.actual_reality: Not all departments count GRFP stipend toward their standard package; some treat it as substitutive, meaning the $37,000 GRFP stipend replaces department funding rather than supplementing it, resulting in zero net financial gain
industry_realities.implication: GRFP winners must explicitly ask programs about additive vs. substitutive policy before relying on the fellowship to increase net compensation

industry_realities.common_belief: A STEM-named degree program automatically qualifies for STEM OPT extension
industry_realities.actual_reality: STEM OPT eligibility is determined solely by the program's CIP code against the ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List; program name is irrelevant — e.g., Information Systems (CIP 52.12xx) is a business program and does not qualify despite sounding like a STEM field
industry_realities.implication: International students must verify the specific CIP code with their DSO before accepting an offer, not after; post-enrollment discovery of ineligibility cannot be remedied

industry_realities.common_belief: International PhD students face the same fellowship landscape as domestic students and should negotiate similarly
industry_realities.actual_reality: International students on F-1/J-1 are excluded from NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART Scholarship, Ford Foundation, and Hertz Foundation fellowships; domestic students can supplement institutional packages with these federal awards, creating a structural funding asymmetry
industry_realities.implication: A department offering identical packages to domestic and international students is effectively underfunding international students; international students should negotiate harder on institutional funding

industry_realities.common_belief: NDSEG is open to all US permanent residents as well as citizens
industry_realities.actual_reality: NDSEG is restricted to US citizens or nationals only; permanent residents are NOT eligible — unlike NSF GRFP and NIH NRSA which include permanent residents
industry_realities.implication: Permanent residents should not include NDSEG in their fellowship strategy and must rely on NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, and other PR-eligible programs

industry_realities.common_belief: Applying for NSF GRFP is best done once enrolled in a PhD program
industry_realities.actual_reality: Applying in the final year of undergraduate study is explicitly allowed and is strategically advantageous in some fields; it also avoids consuming the first of only two eligible application windows post-enrollment
industry_realities.implication: Domestic STEM students should apply for GRFP as senior undergraduates to preserve a second attempt in year one of PhD if needed

industry_realities.common_belief: The SMART Scholarship is a straightforward fellowship with no post-award obligations
industry_realities.actual_reality: SMART Scholarship requires a DoD employment commitment after graduation and summer internship participation; recipients cannot freely pursue academic or private-sector careers until the service obligation is fulfilled
industry_realities.implication: Applicants must assess post-graduation career plans before accepting SMART Scholarship; the service commitment is a binding condition

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Understanding who can access federal fellowships
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes all PhD students at a program compete equally for the same fellowships; does not distinguish citizenship eligibility
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows that NSF GRFP, NIH NRSA, NDSEG, SMART, Ford Foundation, and Hertz are all restricted to US citizens/nationals/PRs (with NDSEG excluding PRs); treats international and domestic fellowship landscapes as structurally distinct
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: International students who assume equal fellowship access will under-negotiate institutional funding and may be materially worse off than domestic peers with equivalent institutional offers

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes any program with 'STEM' or 'technology' in the name qualifies for the 24-month STEM OPT extension; verifies after enrollment
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows that STEM OPT eligibility is determined by CIP code on the ICE/SEVP STEM Designated Degree Program List, not program name; verifies CIP code with DSO before accepting offer
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Post-enrollment discovery that a program does not qualify for STEM OPT limits work authorization to 12 months and cannot be remedied; the difference is 12 months vs. 36 months of legal work authorization

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Assumes GRFP win automatically translates to higher net compensation and uses it as leverage without asking about department policy
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows that GRFP stipend may be substitutive rather than additive at some departments; explicitly asks whether GRFP is additive or substitutive before using it as financial leverage, and pivots to negotiating on conference travel, summer funding, or advisor match if substitutive
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: A GRFP winner who does not ask may receive zero net financial benefit from the fellowship if the department offsets its funding accordingly

junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Waits until enrolled in PhD program to apply for GRFP, treating enrollment as a prerequisite
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Knows GRFP can be applied for in the final year of undergraduate study; applies as a senior undergrad to use the first of two eligible windows before the 12-month enrollment clock begins
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: Applying as a senior undergrad preserves a full second attempt in year one of PhD; failing to do so means a year-one rejection leaves only one remaining eligible window with no further recovery

junior_vs_senior_signals.dimension: Advising international students on fellowship options
junior_vs_senior_signals.naive_pattern: Points international students to the same federal fellowship list as domestic students; does not flag citizenship restrictions
junior_vs_senior_signals.informed_pattern: Immediately identifies that federal fellowships are citizenship-restricted and redirects international students toward institutional fellowships, home country funding programs, Paul & Daisy Soros (for eligible immigrants/PRs), and field-specific non-citizenship-restricted awards
junior_vs_senior_signals.why_it_matters: International students who apply for federal fellowships they are ineligible for waste application effort and may miss deadlines for programs they do qualify for
